# Every entry says why it is expected. A finding outside this file, or an entry the run no longer
# A TIME of 25 hours has no LocalTime.
# Design row 1: three-valued logic; parquet-java returns the null rows under notEq and a one-value notIn.
# Design row 2: parquet-java notIn of more than one value returns every row.
# Design row 3: parquet-java and DuckDB prune a row group holding NaN outside its bounds.
# Design row 4: an int literal on a DECIMAL is the unscaled value; DuckDB compares it as a number.
# Design row 5: an equality literal past the scale is refused.

column3: THROW IllegalArgumentException: Column 'dec_i32' holds a DECIMAL of scale 2 within the INT32 range; the equality literal 0.215 is not a value it can hold

column1: # Design row 6: DuckDB reads nanosecond timestamps as microseconds.
# Design row 7: Float.compare / Double.compare order; DuckDB treats -0.0 as 0.0.
# Design row 8: an unsigned column takes a bit-pattern literal; DuckDB compares the number.
# Design row 9: a byte[] on FLOAT16 is the stored bytes; parquet-java compares the float.
# Design row 10: INTERVAL defines no conversion between components; DuckDB normalises.
# Design row 11: parquet-java orders a Binary on INT96 as a signed big-endian integer.
# Design row 12: parquet-java's Bloom filter tests bytes where its rows test the value.
# Design row 13: a value past its INT(8) annotation; DuckDB narrows it.
# Design row 15: a byte[] of another width on a fixed-width DECIMAL is refused; parquet-java's dictionary and Bloom filter drop the row.

column3: THROW IllegalArgumentException: Column 'dec_flba' holds a byte string of 9 bytes; the equality literal 14 (1 bytes) is not a value it can hold
